name: Skyrush
description: Hersheypark's Intamin wing coaster opened in 2012 and still sets the standard for thrills in Hershey. Riders sit on either side of the track with nothing above or below them as the train climbs to 200 ft (61 m) and plunges down a 212 ft (65 m) first drop, reaching 75 mph (121 km/h) across 3,600 ft (1,100 m) of track. The ride lasts just over a minute and is packed with airtime from start to finish. Min 137cm.

name: Candymonium
description: Candymonium is the Bolliger & Mabillard hypercoaster that rises above Hershey's Chocolatetown and opened in July 2020. At 210 ft (64 m) it is the park's tallest coaster, and with a 216 ft (66 m) first drop and a top speed of 76 mph (122 km/h) it is also the fastest. Over 4,636 ft (1,413 m) of track and about two and a half minutes of ride time it delivers sweeping turns and plenty of floating airtime. Min 137cm.

name: Fahrenheit
description: Fahrenheit is Hersheypark's Intamin coaster that opened in 2008 and is famous for its vertical climb. The train rises 121 ft (37 m) up an almost straight-up lift hill, then tips riders over a 97-degree first drop, steeper than vertical, before racing through loops, corkscrews and dives at up to 58 mph (93 km/h) over 2,700 ft (820 m) of track. Few rides in Pennsylvania are as extreme. Min 137cm.

name: Great Bear
description: Great Bear is Hersheypark's Bolliger & Mabillard inverted coaster, opened in 1998, where riders' feet dangle freely beneath the track. After a 90 ft (27 m) lift hill the train twists through four inversions across 2,800 ft (850 m) of track, in a ride that lasts nearly three minutes. A long-time favourite of coaster fans, it remains one of the park's smoothest thrills. Min 137cm.

name: Storm Runner
description: Storm Runner is an Intamin hydraulic launch coaster that opened in 2004. Instead of a lift hill, the train is fired from the station by a hydraulic launch to 72 mph (116 km/h) and sent up a 150 ft (46 m) peak, then through three inversions over 2,600 ft (790 m) of track. The whole ride is over in under a minute, which makes it one of the most intense experiences in Hersheypark. Min 137cm.

name: Lightning Racer
description: Lightning Racer is a wooden dueling coaster built by Great Coasters International and opened in 2000. Two trains leave the station together and race side by side on twin tracks, each 3,393 ft (1,034 m) long and reaching 51 mph (82 km/h) from a height of 92 ft (28 m). Every ride is a head-to-head contest, so guests often ride twice to see which side wins. Min 122cm.

name: Comet
description: Comet is Hersheypark's classic wooden coaster, built by Philadelphia Toboggan Coasters and open since 1946. In 2026 it celebrates its 80th anniversary. The train rises 84 ft (26 m) and runs at 50 mph (80 km/h) along 3,360 ft (1,020 m) of timber track, in a ride that lasts about a minute and three quarters and shows why traditional wooden coasters are still loved. Min 107cm; riders under 122cm need a supervising companion.

name: sooperdooperLooper
description: sooperdooperLooper is a Schwarzkopf looping coaster that has thrilled guests since opening in 1977. The 70 ft (21 m) steel coaster sends riders around a classic vertical loop along 2,614 ft (797 m) of track, in a ride that lasts around a minute and three quarters. A vintage piece of coaster history that is still popular with guests of all ages. Min 107cm; riders under 122cm need a supervising companion.

name: Laff Trakk
description: Laff Trakk is an indoor spinning coaster built by Maurer that opened in 2015. Its cars rotate freely through a glow-in-the-dark interior, so no two rides are the same. The 51 ft (16 m) coaster reaches 40 mph (64 km/h) over 1,400 ft (430 m) of track in a ride of about a minute and ten seconds, and it is a favourite on hot summer days or in bad weather. Min 107cm.

name: Jolly Rancher Remix
description: Jolly Rancher Remix is a Vekoma Boomerang coaster that opened in 1991 as Sidewinder. The train is pulled backwards up a 116 ft (35 m) lift, released through the station and sent through three inversions at up to 47 mph (76 km/h), then pulled up the second lift and sent through the same course in reverse. Two runs in one short, intense ride. Min 122cm.

name: Trailblazer
description: Trailblazer is a classic Arrow Development mine-train coaster that has been running since 1974. Its winding track wraps around a helix that circles four times, reaching speeds of around 45 mph (72 km/h) on a gentle but fun ride with no inversions. A great first coaster for younger riders and a nostalgic favourite for visitors who grew up with Hersheypark. Min 91cm.

name: Wild Mouse
description: Wild Mouse is a Mack Rides coaster that opened in 1999. Small cars snake around tight 180-degree hairpin turns that feel much faster than they are, so every corner is a surprise. It is a good step up from family rides for guests who are ready for something livelier but not a big coaster. Min 122cm.

name: Cocoa Cruiser
description: Cocoa Cruiser is a Zamperla family gravity coaster that opened in 2014. Its six-car train carries up to 12 riders along a gentle winding track powered only by gravity and a short lift, making it a friendly first coaster for younger guests. No inversions and a low height requirement mean the whole family can ride together. Min 91cm.

name: Breakers Edge Water Coaster
description: Breakers Edge is a ProSlide water coaster in The Boardwalk at Hersheypark, opened in 2018. Rafts are propelled uphill by water jets and swept through twists, turns and drops, a roller-coaster ride that ends with a splash. It is part of the park's summer water-park season. A life jacket is required. Min 107cm.

name: Wildcat's Revenge
description: Wildcat's Revenge is a Rocky Mountain Construction hybrid coaster that opened in 2023, built on the structure of Hersheypark's former Wildcat wooden coaster. It combines a steel track with the existing wooden structure to create a smooth, high-energy ride packed with airtime, and it is one of the park's newest and most talked-about thrills. Min 122cm.
